Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This call is being recorded for claim purposes. Can you confirm
you're comfortable continuing?
A: Yes, that's fine.
Q: Let's start with what happened. Where were you when the collision occurred?
A: I was stopped at a traffic light in Houston, on a main road heading east, waiting for the light to change.
Q: And what happened next?
A: The car behind me didn't stop in time. I felt a hard jolt from the back and my head snapped forward, then back
against the seat.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?
A: Only in my mirror, a second before. It didn't look like it was slowing down much.
Q: Were you able to get out of your vehicle afterward?
A: Yes, but I was sore right away. My right shoulder was throbbing and I had trouble lifting my arm.
Q: Did you seek medical attention?
A: I went to an urgent care clinic that same afternoon. They took X-rays and told me to follow up with an orthopedic
doctor.
Q: Have you had any prior injuries to that shoulder?
A: No, nothing serious. I had some general soreness from working out now and then, but nothing that required
treatment.
Q: Are you currently receiving treatment?
A: Yes, I have physical therapy twice a week, and I'm still limited in how far I can reach overhead.
Q: Thank you. Is there anything you'd like to add that I haven't asked about?
A: Just that my car is still at the repair shop, and I've had to rely on a rental, which has been a hassle.
Q: Understood. Thank you for your cooperation today.
</page>
